classification.difficultyReason: Use vertically opposite angles to establish the combined central-angle sum, then subtract it from the total angle sums of three triangles.

content.prompt: Find the sum of all six angles shaded in the figure below.

spec.description: Three triangles meet at one central vertex. Their rays form exactly three straight lines; the six noncentral angles are shaded.
spec.mathematics: The three central triangle angles alternate around the common vertex and total 180 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No answers, labels or numerical givens are visible.

answer.short:
$360^\circ$.

The three central angles total $180^\circ$; subtract them from the angle sums of three triangles.
answer.worked:
Let the three central triangle angles be $x$, $y$ and $z$. Their vertically opposite angles are equal to them, so

$$\begin{align*}2(x+y+z)&=360^\circ\\x+y+z&=180^\circ.\end{align*}$$

Let $S$ be the sum of the six shaded angles. Using the angle sums of the three triangles,

$$\begin{align*}S&=3\times180^\circ-(x+y+z)\\S&=540^\circ-180^\circ\\S&=360^\circ.\end{align*}$$
